Help? Advice? Got teku running with no problems I'm going to convert some of your docs to markdown if you don't mind <@!573787335796326400> That's a weird thing, I cannot confirm the teku deposits ``` You are about to submit 64 transactions of 32.000000000 Eth. [y/n]^M^M^M^M^M^M^M^M^M^M^M^M^C ``` Pressing `[ENTER]` sends `^M` instead of return I mean `^M` is the carriage return, but why does Teku not accept it as one? `Are you sure you want to continue? [y/n]yes^My^Myyy^M^M^M^C` Nevemind, that was an issue with `zsh` > I'm going to convert some of your docs to markdown if you don't mind <@!573787335796326400> <@557201004060213248> Sure, but note that they're also being worked on to go up on our official Teku docs pages in the next day or two, so don't feel you need to. My notes are highly unofficial, lol 😂 ok added 64 teku validators to rebalance the network a bit 🙂 might be a bug in eth1data on one of the clients https://schlesi.beaconcha.in/block/133567 https://schlesi.beaconcha.in/block/133568 back to back blocks with same deposit count vote but different block hash and the block hash from 133567 doesn't exist in goerli same deposit root too seems that prysm might have a bug here cc: <@!363800010518822915> We don't have a custom graffitti flag, so probably not us unless someone's changed the source. proposer 42, deposit count 421.. shame we missed out on a 42 & 420 combo yeah, the sigp graffitis point to the correct block on goerli seems the ones with prysm graffiti I found point to a non-existent block on goerli last validator activation was in the 200s and 16 hours ago don't tihnk new deposits are getting in riht now def a shame. I created a new validator about an hour ago, will keep an eye on it no deposits are coming in blocks. don't think new eth1data is getting in I have two teku vals waiting to join the party It’s not necessarily a bug. Prysm will generate a random vote if it’s not connected to eth1 I would check with the operator to see what flags they are using, if there is a good connection with eth1 they have the correct deposit count and deposit root but incorrect block so it seems they are connected to eth1 it might be a re-org in goerli actually nvm Or they were connected to eth1 but no longer that wont come up if its a re-org and are giving a consistent eth1 block root (across multiple votes/nodes) just not an existent one but you're right, I don't have much more info than that to go off of Can you give an example? The ones you linked just a moment ago point to eth1 blocks follow the eth1 block root from this one https://schlesi.beaconcha.in/block/133567 Ok here's one tagged as prysm -- https://schlesi.beaconcha.in/block/133566 with same block root the votes between prysm and lighthouse are getting same deposit root and deposit count so something small seems off i know <@!557201004060213248> runs some of the nodes. not sure who the other operators are funny thing to try to debug. We can't spin up prysm validators to try to reproduce on the network because we won't get processed in! (seems like prysm and lighthouse are near 50/50 split on the network so if yuo account for randomly missed blocks, the network is having trouble coming to consensus on new eth1data) This is the first time hearing about this type of issue . Topaz works fine https://beacon.etherscan.io/slot/201457 Need more information to assess it If there was a Goerli fork, this kind of thing might resolve itself in the next voting round did some digging this first came up here https://schlesi.beaconcha.in/block/133120 before that lighthouse + prysm had the same eth1data yeah, hard to say from here likelihood of a goerli fork at 1000 blocks deep is almost non-existent due to the clique signing alg teku agreeing on the 0xce block https://schlesi.beaconcha.in/block/133578 I suspect most prysm nodes are querying the prysm eth1 endpoint. could check that that is providing good data That might be the case although its hard to know, it might be an issue with our eth1 block cache if thats the case restarting prysm nodes should fix it <@!557201004060213248> can give that a try when he is up I'm back. Looking at this now. One thing that's on top of my mind, is we haven't updated proposer's eth1 voting scheme since v0.9.0 of the spec. Not sure if this issue could be attributed due to difference in terms of how proposer votes for eth1 data I dont think so that block hash doesn't exist at all even if our proposer voting scheme is slightly different, we should not be voting for a non-existent block Right. It does sound like what Preston has described. Our proposer votes for a random block if it's not correctly conencted with eth1 it's probably bad eth1 info from the eth1 node we'll turn down our public eth1 endpoint for the official MC net this isn't cache related actually yeah it could be cache related https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/cb045dd0e360192fb9e46314b3954f3bf58f4871/beacon-chain/powchain/block_reader.go#L101 the weird part is the correctness of the other two fields ok so i think Prysm has a bug where it is eagerly caching all of these eth1 blocks. When it saw this block, it immediately cached it in memory. There could he been a reorg of distance 1 and the cache might not have been updated. This cache needs to be reworked or disable for mainnet ahhh that's interesting that is my immediate thinking anyway, i don't have supporting evidence yet if this is correct, a restart will fix this so that would unblock us for now to include new deposits yep or waiting 1024 slots will fix it whenever the round changes solid theory nonetheless and something to investigate regardless breaking for some dinner. have a nice weekend everyone! yes, as Terence said, we haven't looked at this routine seriously since 0.9 or even earlier
